title: A Clock for the Regiment
premise: In 1746, Ansel Hartwell has spent six years living as a boy to keep her place as mapmaker Elias Hartwell's apprentice, and now she alone holds the half-finished atlas of the borderlands he died surveying. When a crown census taker named Verity Cole arrives asking questions the answers to could unmask Ansel, expose the atlas's forbidden details, and condemn the workshop's found family of misfits, the two women strike an uneasy bargain: Verity's silence in exchange for the truth Elias died protecting. As soldiers close in and the atlas becomes evidence in a conspiracy neither fully understands, Ansel must choose between finishing her master's work and destroying it to save the people she loves. In the end she completes the atlas, smuggles it to the one honest official left, and claims her own name publicly for the first time — losing the workshop, but gaining a family that knows and chooses her anyway.
about_author: Ivo Dunmore is the pen name of a former archival cartographer who spent a decade restoring eighteenth-century survey maps in provincial record offices. Their novels are known for turning dusty documents into ticking clocks.

chapters.title: The Question Too Many
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. In the winter workshop, Ansel inks the atlas's final border plates while the household — deaf engraver Tam, runaway housekeeper Mrs. Quill, and old master's widow — prepares for the census. Verity Cole's visit begins routinely until she asks how many sons Elias Hartwell had. Ansel's lie lands, but Verity's eyes linger. Beat: dread beneath routine.

chapters.title: What Elias Died Drawing
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV, with a flashback to her master's final fevered return from the marsh survey. She discovers a sealed folio hidden in the atlas's binding: the border drawn differently than the crown's version, dated three days before his death. Beat: the work she loved becomes a weapon she didn't ask to hold.

chapters.title: Verity's Second Visit
chapters.summary: Verity's POV. Officially verifying the census, Verity returns, and the two women circle each other over tea and triangulation. Verity reveals she suspects Elias was murdered for what he mapped, and that her own superiors sent her to bury it. Beat: wary recognition — two women both performing roles they didn't choose.

chapters.title: The Household Holds
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. A garrison officer arrives demanding the workshop's survey records for the crown's rival map. Ansel forges a duplicate set overnight with Tam's help, and the household closes ranks around her secret without being told it. Beat: found family solidifying in shared danger.

chapters.title: Marsh Country
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, Ansel and Verity. The two travel together to the marsh where Elias died, retracing his final survey. They find his buried benchmark stone and evidence he was followed. Verity admits she reported Ansel's irregularities before she understood them — a confession that shatters the fragile trust. Beat: betrayal in the rain.

chapters.title: The Name on the Door
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Back home, the garrison has posted a warrant naming 'the Hartwell apprentice.' Mrs. Quill urges Ansel to flee as a girl and abandon the atlas; Ansel refuses — finishing the work is the only identity she trusts. Tam, nearly arrested, is hidden in the cellar. Beat: identity as loyalty, not disguise.

chapters.title: Ink and Ashes
chapters.summary: Verity's POV. Verity is ordered to lead the raid on the workshop at week's end. She burns her own commission file to buy time and rides through the night to warn Ansel, knowing it ends her career and possibly her life. Beat: loyalty to truth over institution.

chapters.title: The Last Plate
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. With the raid hours away, Ansel inks the final plate — the true border, Elias's evidence, and her own signature: Ansel Hartwell, in full. The household packs the atlas into a survey case while soldiers' lanterns appear on the lane. Beat: the quiet triumph of self-naming before the storm.

chapters.title: The Workshop Stands, the Workshop Falls
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, climax. The raid comes; Verity stalls the officer with forged orders while Ansel escapes through the marsh with the atlas, guided by the benchmarks she can now read. The workshop burns; Mrs. Quill and Tam scatter to safehouses. Ansel reaches the one incorruptible surveyor-general's clerk. Beat: sacrifice, pursuit, near-loss.

chapters.title: A Clock for the Regiment
chapters.summary: Verity and Ansel's shared POV, epilogue. Months later, the atlas is entered into evidence; the border inquiry opens and the garrison's commander falls. The workshop is a ruin, but the household reunites in a rented room above a print shop, where Ansel — under her own name, apprenticed to no one — begins a new map. Verity knocks at the door with her own trunk. Beat: resolution — truth kept, family chosen, time finally their own.
